newsitem.title: THAILAND: Northwest Thai unit sees revenue up 14 pct.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Thai unit sees revenue up 14 pct.

text.p: Northwest Airlines Corp's Thai unit said on Tuesday it expects revenue in 1997 to grow about 14 percent despite the country's struggling economy.

"We hope that 1997 will be another successful year for Northwest although there will be many unfavourable factors such as the sluggish economy," Sarathool Monthienvichienchai, general manager of Thailand for Northwest, told a news conference.
In 1996, the net profit for Northwest's Thai operation rose 13 percent to more than one billion baht ($38.46 million), said Sarathool, declining to give an exact figure.
He said the sluggish economy and slumping stock market will weaken Thai people's demand for overseas travel.
"I am confident that our existing marketing and sales staff will find the ways to overcome those unfavourable conditions to achieve the target," Sarathool said.
Northwest currently operates seven passenger flights a week from Thailand and has no plans in the near term to increase that amount, he said.
"The current flights are sufficient to meet the demand here," he said.
The baht's recent depreciation against the U.S. dollar will have some impact on the number of passengers going to the United States, he said.
"But the impact of U.S. routes will be offset by the expected increase in number of Thai passengers to Japan as a result of the baht's strength against the yen," Sarathool said.
He said the number of Thai passengers travelling to Japan rose by five percent in January compared with negative growth last year.
